problem_motivation.content: Ferroelectricity in 2D systems is challenging because reduced dimensionality enhances depolarizing fields.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Despite those advantages, ferroelectricity in a 2D system poses a unique challenge; the reduced dimensionality enhances the depolarizing fields [9, 10].

prior_approach.content: Prior work theoretically proposed and experimentally demonstrated sliding ferroelectricity in hBN and TMDC systems.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This form of ferroelectricity was first theoretically proposed [17] and later experimentally demonstrated in systems such as parallel-stacked bilayer hBN [18, 19] and various transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) [20–25].

prior_approach.content: Previous studies used piezoelectric force microscopy to visualize domains and switching.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM) has been used to visualize interfacial ferroelectric domains and detect switching behavior under an external electric field [18, 21].

prior_approach.content: Previous studies used DC transport with graphene charge sensing to probe sliding ferroelectricity.
prior_approach.evidence_span: DC transport measurements have also been used to investigate sliding ferroelectricity [18, 21]. In these experiments, graphene has been employed as a charge sensor, where shifts in its doping reveal the built-in interlayer potential associated with ferroelectric polarization.

prior_approach.content: Capacitance-based sensing was previously used to study spontaneous polarization in bilayer WTe2.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This method was recently used to investigate spontaneous polarization in bilayer WTe2 as a function of the out-of-plane electric field and carrier density [26].

prior_approach.content: Superconducting microwave resonators were previously used to probe quantum capacitance, superfluid stiffness, and microwave losses in 2D materials.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Their implementations have already been used to probe quantum capacitance [27, 28], superfluid stiffness [29–31], and microwave losses [32].

prior_approach.content: Prior work by Aebischer provided the inductance formula used for the geometry.
prior_approach.evidence_span: We have calculated the inductance for our geometry from the formula provided in the paper by Aebischer [41].

prior_approach.content: Prior work by Mi et al. supplied the adopted low-pass filter design.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The design of the filter is adopted from the work by Mi et al. [40].

rejected_alternative.content: Unlike PFM-style direction measurements, the study does not directly measure polarization direction, instead relying on reproducible hysteretic capacitance sensitive to net polarization.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In our work, while we did not perform a direction measurement for polarization like PFM, we observed clear and reproducible hysteretic behaviour in the capacitance in the twisted WSe2 devices.

rejected_alternative.content: In contrast to PFM, SHG, and transport methods, the authors position their technique as targeting high-frequency dielectric properties and loss mechanisms via time-domain measurements.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: This microwave cavity-based approach complements existing ferroelectric characterization methods such as PFM, SHG, and transport measurements. In contrast to these methods, our technique can be used to probe the high-frequency dielectric properties and loss mechanisms present in a ferroelectric system by time-domain measurements.

inspiration_source.content: The low-pass filter design was adopted from prior work by Mi et al.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The design of the filter is adopted from the work by Mi et al. [40].

causal_claim.content: Breaking inversion and out-of-plane mirror symmetries in a bilayer creates net out-of-plane polarization via interfacial charge transfer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When two monolayer flakes are stacked in a configuration that breaks both the inversion symmetry and the out-of-plane symmetry of the bilayer, a net out-of-plane polarization emerges due to interfacial charge transfer.

causal_claim.content: Sliding switches between equivalent stackings with opposite polarization rather than generating ferroelectricity directly.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Instead, sliding switches the system between energetically equivalent stacking configurations with opposite polarization[15, 16].

causal_claim.content: Real susceptibility changes shift resonator frequency, while imaginary susceptibility changes resonator loss.
causal_claim.evidence_span: On one hand, the real part of ˜ϵ modifies the capacitance of the heterostructure and thus causes a shift in the resonator frequency. On the other hand, the imaginary part of ˜ϵ modifies the losses in the resonator.

causal_claim.content: Changes in polarization under applied out-of-plane field change heterostructure capacitance, which is detected as a cavity frequency shift.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With the change in polarization in t-WSe2 upon application of an external out-of-plane electric field, the capacitance of the heterostructure changes, which are detected by the change in the resonant frequency of the cavity.

causal_claim.content: Microwave-field interaction with ferroelectric domain walls induces dissipation and lowers cavity internal quality factor.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Furthermore, as the microwave electric field interacts with the ferroelectric domain walls, it induces dissipation by moving these domain walls, which is reflected in a reduction of the internal quality factor of the cavity.

causal_claim.content: After relaxation, favorable MX and XM regions grow while unfavorable XX regions shrink.
causal_claim.evidence_span: After relaxation, the energetically favorable MX and XM regions grow in size, and the unfavorable XX regions shrink in size [34].

causal_claim.content: Applying an out-of-plane electric field favors one stacking order and expands the corresponding domains while shrinking the opposite ones.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When an external out-of-plane electric field is applied, it couples to the layer polarization, energetically favoring one stacking order over the other. When an upward electric field is applied, it favors the MX domains with upward polarization, causing MX domains to expand and XM domains to shrink. The reverse effect happens when the direction of the electric field is reversed

causal_claim.content: At higher electric field, domain-wall pinning reduces polarizability and capacitance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At a higher electric field, most of the domain walls get pinned by defects, impurities, or lattice inhomogeneities in the system[20]. This results in a decrease in the polarizability of the system, which, in turn, reduces the capacitance of the system.

causal_claim.content: Microwave-driven domain-wall motion is dissipative and changes the cavity internal quality factor.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This domain wall motion under the microwave electric field is not purely elastic, resulting in dissipation in the system, which changes the internal quality factor of the cavity.

causal_claim.content: Control experiments show the observed hysteresis originates from twisted WSe2 rather than hBN layers or their interface.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Together, these control experiments demonstrate that the hysteresis observed in our main device originates from the t-WSe2 heterostructure and is not due to the hBN layers or their interface.

causal_claim.content: Because the measurement is sensitive to net polarization and domain-area fractions, it is suited to probing moiré sliding ferroelectrics where full monodomain switching is impossible.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Our measurement is sensitive to the net polarization of the system and, consequently, to changes in the relative area fractions of the MX and XM domains. In a real moir´e-based sliding ferroelectric system, it is not possible to achieve a fully monodomain state. Therefore, our measurement scheme is well-suited for probing ferroelectricity in such systems.

causal_claim.content: Approximate formulas and simulation limitations caused the mismatch between lumped-element and finite-element traces.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This discrepancy arises because the formulas used to calculate the capacitance and inductance are approximate, and the finite element simulation also has its limitations.

causal_claim.content: Fixing the bare resonant frequency ensures that observed resonance shifts come only from capacitive loading, not from changes in ω0.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This ensures that any observed shift in the resonant frequency arises solely from the capacitive loading due to C2, and not from variations in ω0.

causal_claim.content: The fitting procedure enables extraction of effective capacitance and internal quality factor.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This fitting procedure allows us to extract both the effective capacitance C2 of the heterostructure and the internal quality factor Qi, which reflects the loss mechanisms in the system.

causal_claim.content: Keeping electric field constant during the fast-axis sweep prevents domain reconfiguration and thus eliminates hysteresis.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The electric field remains constant during the sweep in both directions along the fast axis. As a result, the domain configuration does not change during the sweep for either direction, and no hysteresis is observed.

causal_claim.content: Control measurements confirm that hysteresis originates from twisted WSe2.
causal_claim.evidence_span: To confirm that hysteresis originates from twisted WSe2, a control device is measured.

causal_claim.content: Choosing an hBN-hBN twist angle near 23 degrees prevents sliding-ferroelectricity-driven response from the hBN-hBN interface.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The targeted twist angle between the two hBN flakes was ∼23◦to ensure that ferroelectricity does not arise from the hBN-hBN interface due to sliding ferroelectricity[18].

causal_claim.content: Absence of hysteresis in the hBN-hBN control shows that hBN or the hBN-hBN interface does not contribute to the observed ferroelectric response.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The corresponding internal quality factor measurements Qi, shown in Fig. S8c and S8d, also do not show hysteresis, confirming that the hBN–hBN interface or hBN does not contribute to the observed ferroelectric response.

mechanism_principle.content: Sliding ferroelectricity arises from stacking-induced breaking of inversion and out-of-plane mirror symmetries, not ionic displacement within a monolayer.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In this mechanism, ferroelectric polarization arises not from ionic displacements within a monolayer but from the stacking-induced breaking of inversion and out-of-plane mirror symmetries in the system.

mechanism_principle.content: Lack of inversion and out-of-plane mirror symmetry enables interlayer hybridization and charge transfer, producing net polarization.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Because of the lack of inversion symmetry and out-of-plane mirror symmetry, interlayer hybridization occurs between the occupied bands of one layer and the unoccupied bands of the other layer. This leads to charge transfer between the layers [33], resulting in a net out-of-plane polarization [18, 20, 21, 34].

mechanism_principle.content: Coexisting MX and XM domains allow mobile domain walls, increasing effective polarizability and capacitance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This corresponds to the situation where both MX and XM regions coexist, with opposite out-of-plane polarization... The domain walls in this region are free to move, which increases the effective polarizability of the system.

mechanism_principle.content: Asymmetry of hysteresis for positive and negative fields arises from unequal top and bottom interfaces and different electrode work functions.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This asymmetry mainly arises from differences between the top and bottom interfaces, such as the top hBN/WSe2 or hBN/metal interface and the bottom hBN/WSe2 or hBN/metal interface... In addition, the top and bottom electrodes are fabricated from different superconducting materials with distinct work functions (MoRe for the top electrode and NbTiN for the bottom electrode), which can further contribute to the observed asymmetry [39].

mechanism_principle.content: No hysteresis in that sweep occurs because the electric field stays constant along the fast-axis sweeps, so domain configuration does not change.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The electric field remains constant during the sweep in both directions along the fast axis. As a result, the domain configuration does not change during the sweep for either direction, and no hysteresis is observed.

mechanism_principle.content: At low electric field, freely moving domain walls cause larger oscillations and higher loss; at high field, pinned walls oscillate less.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At low electric field, the domain walls are free to move... Therefore, the system becomes more lossy at a lower electric field... At high electric field, most of the domain walls are pinned and respond less to the microwave electric field

mechanism_principle.content: At low fields, mixed domains relax by domain-wall annihilation to lower-energy states, reducing polarizability and increasing Qi; at high fields, near-monodomain pinned states stay stable.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At low electric fields, a mixed-domain state with mobile domain walls exists in the system. When the gate sweep is halted, the previously evolving domain walls gradually relax towards a lower-energy stable configuration by annihilating them. This reduces the effective polarizability of the system, leading to a gradual decrease in capacitance and a simultaneous increase in the Qi. In contrast, at a high electric field, the system is driven into a nearly monodomain state, and most of the domain walls are strongly pinned. Consequently, the capacitance and Qi remain constant over time.

mechanism_principle.content: The mismatch is explained by approximate capacitance/inductance formulas and finite-element simulation limitations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This discrepancy arises because the formulas used to calculate the capacitance and inductance are approximate, and the finite element simulation also has its limitations.

mechanism_principle.content: No hysteresis occurs because constant electric field leaves the domain configuration unchanged during the sweep.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The electric field remains constant during the sweep in both directions along the fast axis. As a result, the domain configuration does not change during the sweep for either direction, and no hysteresis is observed.

hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, the cavity-based technique is extended to probe ferroelectricity in small-angle (0.1◦) twisted WSe2 (t-WSe2) using a superconducting coplanar waveguide (SCPW) cavity.

evidence_result.content: Measured capacitance shows hysteresis versus both top-gate and bottom-gate voltage.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Fig. 3b and 3c show the measured capacitance with the upward and downward sweep of the top gate voltage and the bottom gate voltage, respectively. There is hysteresis in capacitance with both gate voltages.

evidence_result.content: A capacitance peak appears at small electric field/low gate voltage.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For a small electric field or low gate voltage, a peak in capacitance is observed.

evidence_result.content: Low-capacitance region and hysteresis appear when sweeping along the electric-field axis, with threshold initial fields and coercive field around 0.14 V/nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A region of lower capacitance appears in the low electric field region, and hysteresis occurs when the direction of the fast axis is reversed... For the upward and downward electric field sweep, the minimum electric fields are ∼0.16 V/nm and ∼0.21 V/nm, respectively. From the hysteresis loop, we estimate the coercive field to be ∼0.14 V/nm.

evidence_result.content: The measured coercive field agrees with literature values for similar devices.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our result is in good agreement with the previously reported values.

evidence_result.evidence_span: No hysteresis is observed if the sweep is taken with the axis perpendicular to the electric field as the fast axis and axis parallel to the electric field as the slow axis

evidence_result.evidence_span: In the region where the capacitance increases, the internal quality factor of the cavity decreases; conversely, the internal quality factor of the cavity increases as the capacitance decreases.

evidence_result.content: Changing microwave power alters capacitance more in the high-electric-field region than in the low-field region.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In the higher electric field region, there is a change in the capacitance between the two powers. However, in the low electric field region, the change is less.

evidence_result.content: In one regime capacitance decreases and Qi increases over time toward saturation, while in another both remain nearly constant.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The capacitance decreases with time and eventually saturates... Similarly, Qi increases with time and saturates... Both capacitance and Qi in this region remain almost constant with time.

evidence_result.content: Control hBN-hBN device shows no hysteresis in capacitance or Qi versus electric field.
evidence_result.evidence_span: No hysteresis is observed in either the capacitance or Qi with the electric field.

evidence_result.content: The main observation is hysteresis in capacitance and internal quality factor versus out-of-plane electric field, consistent with ferroelectric switching.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The observed hysteresis in capacitance and internal quality factor (Qi) as a function of the applied out-of-plane electric field is consistent with ferroelectric switching dynamics.

evidence_result.content: The measured cavity response qualitatively matches the simulation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The | ˜S21| data qualitatively match well with the simulation.

evidence_spans: No hysteresis is observed if the sweep is taken with the axis perpendicular to the electric field as the fast axis and axis parallel to the electric field as the slow axis
No hysteresis is observed in capacitance or in Qi between two sweep directions.

evidence_result.content: Capacitance and cavity internal quality factor Qi are anticorrelated: where capacitance increases, Qi decreases, and vice versa; correspondingly, hysteresis is also observed in the monolayer-WSe2 device Qi data.
evidence_spans: In the region where the capacitance increases, the internal quality factor of the cavity decreases; conversely, the internal quality factor of the cavity increases as the capacitance decreases.
A similar hysteresis is observed in Qi also.
The observed hysteresis in capacitance and internal quality factor (Qi) as a function of the applied out-of-plane electric field is consistent with ferroelectric switching dynamics.

evidence_result.content: Changing microwave power modifies capacitance more strongly in the high-electric-field region than in the low-field region.
evidence_spans: In the higher electric field region, there is a change in the capacitance between the two powers. However, in the low electric field region, the change is less.

evidence_result.content: Time dependence is regime dependent: in one regime, capacitance decreases with time and saturates while Qi increases with time and saturates, whereas in another regime both capacitance and Qi remain nearly constant over time.
evidence_spans: The capacitance decreases with time and eventually saturates... Similarly, Qi increases with time and saturates... Both capacitance and Qi in this region remain almost constant with time.

evidence_result.content: In the hBN-hBN control device, no hysteresis is observed in either capacitance or Qi versus electric field.
evidence_spans: No hysteresis is observed in either the capacitance or Qi with the electric field.
There is no hysteresis in the capacitance.
The corresponding internal quality factor measurements Qi, shown in Fig. S8c and S8d, also do not show hysteresis

evidence_result.content: The measured cavity response |S21| qualitatively matches the simulation, and a 180° phase shift around the peak indicates half-wave (λ/2) cavity behavior.
evidence_spans: The | ˜S21| data qualitatively match well with the simulation.
In Fig. S5b a 180-degree phase shift is observed around the peak, which is characteristic of a half-wave (λ/2) cavity.

evidence_result.content: At the reference point, the extracted capacitance was 37.207 fF and the internal quality factor Qi was 1736.092, with fitting uncertainties much smaller than the extracted values.
evidence_spans: The extracted capacitance and internal quality factor from the fitting are C2 = 37.207 fF and Qi = 1736.092.
Therefore, the fitting uncertainties of the extracted capacitance and internal quality factor from the fitting are of the order of magnitude lower than the extracted values.

constraint.content: WSe2 must remain well away from parallel stacking with both the top and bottom hBN layers; parallel stacking alone does not guarantee strong interfacial coupling or ferroelectricity, and the observed response may depend on device-specific details.
evidence_spans: Therefore, WSe2 is well away from the parallel-stacking configuration with both the hBNs.

At the same time, we note that parallel stacking alone does not guarantee strong interfacial coupling or the emergence of ferroelectricity, and the observed response may depend on device-specific details.

constraint.content: In real moiré-based sliding ferroelectric systems, complete switching into a fully monodomain state is not achievable.
evidence_spans: It is important to note that in moir´e-based ferroelectric systems, complete switching into a monodomain state is not achievable.
In a real moir´e-based sliding ferroelectric system, it is not possible to achieve a fully monodomain state.
